tasks.description:
**Question.** How weak a coherent motion signal can a person still see the direction of? (A human adaptation of the monkeys' task.)

**What is on the screen.** A yellow fixation point alone for 500 ms, then [[param:stimulus_duration]] of stochastic random dots in a [[param:aperture_dva]] black disc centred on it. On each frame a proportion of dots (the correlation) is replotted a fixed step along the horizontal axis; the rest are replotted at random.

**What the subject does.** Keeps looking at the fixation point (asked, not checked: this set uses no eye tracker), then after the dots go off presses the right or left arrow within [[param:response_timeout]]. The fixation point turns green or red for 300 ms.

**Varied.** Correlation, one of [[param:coherences_pct]] %, and direction (right or left), 15 trials of each per block in random order.

**Measured.** Proportion correct at each correlation; the analysis fits the paper's Weibull function for threshold (82 % correct) and slope. At 0 % the 'correct' key is the trial's nominal direction, so feedback is right on a random half.

**What it can and cannot show.** A psychometric function for this observer and display. It cannot reproduce the paper's neuron-versus-behaviour comparison: that needs an MT recording made during the same trials, and the paper's subjects were monkeys whose aperture, axis and speed were matched to each neuron.
notes: Adaptation: the paper tested monkeys reporting with a saccade; keys, the 500-ms fixation period, 300-ms feedback and 1-s interval are ASSUMED (configs/task.yaml).
Axis (horizontal), speed 6 dva/s, aperture 10 dva and the correlation set are ASSUMED; the paper tailored them to each MT neuron.
Dot count is one frame at the booth rig's 60 Hz: 16.7 dots/deg²/s over a 20 x 20 dva plotting field, of which only dots inside the aperture are drawn.
Inks: yellow fixation point (#ffff00, paper p. 4748), white dots and targets, black aperture disc, on the window's mid-grey (the paper's whole display was dark: a deviation in the config).
Human set, no eye tracker: fixation is instructed only, so eye movements toward or with the dots are not excluded (unlike the paper's search-coil-enforced 1.25° window).

tasks.description:
**Question.** The paper's trial: can the monkey report the direction of a weak motion signal placed in a neuron's receptive field?

**What is on the screen.** A yellow fixation point; after fixation is acquired and held 300 ms, [[param:stimulus_duration]] of random dots in an aperture over an example receptive field. Then the fixation point and the dots go off and two targets appear on the motion axis, [[param:target_ecc_dva]] either side of fixation. Dots and targets are never on together.

**What the subject does.** Holds gaze inside the fixation window through the dots (checked by the eye tracker; leaving it ends the trial as FIX_BREAK), then saccades to the target on the side of the motion within [[param:response_timeout]].

**Varied.** Correlation, one of [[param:coherences_pct]] %, and direction (preferred or null), 15 trials of each per block. Three wrong choices in a row in one direction start correction trials in that direction (excluded from analysis).

**Measured.** Which target the saccade lands on (CORRECT, WRONG, MISSED, NO_CHOICE). Juice for a correct choice; a [[param:error_timeout]] time-out after a wrong one; at 0 % a random half of trials pay.

**What it can and cannot show.** A monkey psychometric function on this rig. The neurometric half (MT spike counts on the same trials) needs a recording system this folder does not run; the aperture, axis and speed here are example values, not matched to a neuron.
notes: Aperture position (6, -4) dva, size 7 dva, axis and speed are EXAMPLE values, ASSUMED; the paper matched them to each MT neuron.

Paper values: 2-s display, 1.25-dva fixation window, 2.1-s decision window, correction trials after 3 errors. Acquire 5 s/200 ms, 300-ms hold, 200-ms landing sample, 1.5-s time-out, 1-s interval, target eccentricity and windows are ASSUMED.
Dot count is one frame at the example rig's 120 Hz (16.7 dots/deg²/s over a 20 x 20 dva field, drawn only inside the aperture).
Window radii are drawn as radii (the code uses them as circle radii).
Inks: yellow fixation point (#ffff00, paper p. 4748), white dots and targets (target colour ASSUMED), black aperture disc, on the window's mid-grey.
